topic: Strange borders countdown: Thai-Lao bridge to India's four-layer enclave
hook: Your car can swap sides of the road halfway across a bridge, and that is only border number seven in this countdown.
title: 7 Weird Borders, and India's Is the Strangest
description:
Cars swap sides of the road on the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, a Spanish town sits inside France, and a German town runs on Swiss francs. This countdown ends on India's strangest border, a patch of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh. Every place is real and you can find each one on a map.

#borders #geography #facts

scenes.narration: Your car can swap sides of the road halfway across a bridge, and that is only border number seven in this countdown.
scenes.headline: Cars Swap Sides

scenes.narration: Today I will show you seven real borders that make no sense, each one stranger than the one before it.
scenes.headline: 7 Impossible Borders

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see a patch of India inside Bangladesh, inside India, inside Bangladesh, all on a single map.
scenes.headline: India Inside Bangladesh

scenes.narration: Every place in this video is real, and you can search for each one on your phone tonight.
scenes.headline: All Of It Is Real

scenes.narration: We start on a river bridge in Asia where drivers have to change which side of the road they use.
scenes.headline: Start: A River Bridge

scenes.narration: Stay until the very end, because number one took a treaty, a midnight handover and years of waiting to fix.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Wild
scenes.sub: A treaty and a midnight handover

scenes.narration: Number seven: the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, where your car swaps sides of the road right above a river.
scenes.headline: Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge

scenes.narration: The bridge crosses the Mekong river, joining Nong Khai in Thailand with the Laotian capital Vientiane on the other bank.
scenes.headline: Over The Mekong

scenes.narration: Thailand drives on the left side of the road, just like India does, so Indian viewers would feel at home.
scenes.headline: Thailand: Left

scenes.narration: Laos drives on the right, like most of the world. So the two countries follow opposite rules.
scenes.headline: Laos: Right

scenes.narration: Now think about the problem. A car arrives from one country and has to leave on the other country's side.
scenes.headline: Opposite Rules Meet

scenes.narration: The switch happens on the bridge itself, not at some normal junction on land, which is why the bridge is famous.
scenes.headline: Swap On The Bridge

scenes.narration: Road signs and markings tell drivers when to change sides, and the whole stream of traffic moves across together.
scenes.headline: Signs Guide You

scenes.narration: This bridge opened in 1994, and it was the first one built across the lower Mekong river.
scenes.headline: Opened In 1994

scenes.narration: Before that, people mostly crossed the water by boat. Later a short railway link was added as well.
scenes.headline: Boat, Then Bridge

scenes.narration: Picture the drive: left side, then a swap, then right side, all in a few minutes over water.
scenes.headline: Left, Swap, Right

scenes.narration: That one can be solved with paint and signs. The next border is stuck because of a treaty from 1659.
scenes.headline: Paint Can't Fix This

scenes.narration: Number six: Llívia, a Spanish town that sits inside France with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Llívia: Spain In France

scenes.narration: On a map of the Pyrenees, you see France everywhere, and then one small patch that is still Spain.
scenes.headline: A Spanish Island

scenes.narration: The reason goes back to 1659, when Spain handed a group of villages in this area over to France.
scenes.headline: The 1659 Deal

scenes.narration: Llívia was counted as a town, not a village, so it was left out of the deal and stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: Today a road that was kept neutral under that old treaty links the town to the rest of Spain.
scenes.headline: A Neutral Road

scenes.narration: So you can drive out of Llívia, and within a short distance you are surrounded by France.
scenes.headline: Spain, Then France

scenes.narration: A deal made more than three and a half centuries ago still decides which flag flies over this town.
scenes.headline: Old Deal, Same Flag

scenes.narration: It is a tiny place, but it is a perfect example of how one word in a treaty can change a map.
scenes.headline: One Word Changed It

scenes.narration: Next, a piece of America that you can only reach by road if you drive through Canada first.
scenes.headline: America Via Canada

scenes.narration: Number five: Point Roberts, a small American community that hangs off the bottom of Canada like a loose thread.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: It sits on the tip of a peninsula, just south of the 49th parallel, which is the US and Canada border line.
scenes.headline: South Of The 49th

scenes.narration: Because the border follows that line on the map, the tip of the peninsula ended up cut off from America.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By A Line

scenes.narration: To drive from Point Roberts to the rest of Washington state, you must pass through Canada by road.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: That means a border crossing into Canada, and another crossing back into the United States, just to reach an American city.
scenes.headline: Two Crossings

scenes.narration: Locals live in the United States, but the road to the rest of their state runs through another country.
scenes.headline: Home, Via Canada

scenes.narration: On a map it looks like a mistake, but it is a real community with real homes and real people.
scenes.headline: Looks Like A Mistake

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like these, subscribe to the channel, because the next four get even weirder.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: And the next one is a lake that three countries have never agreed how to divide.
scenes.headline: A Lake Without A Line

scenes.narration: Number four: Lake Constance, a huge lake where three countries never agreed on a final border line.
scenes.headline: Lake Constance

scenes.narration: The lake sits where Germany, Switzerland and Austria meet, and it is big enough to have ferries and ports.
scenes.headline: Three Countries Meet

scenes.narration: On the land around it, every border is clear. On the water, no one ever signed one agreed line.
scenes.headline: No Agreed Line

scenes.narration: The three countries have never agreed whether the lake should be shared or divided.
scenes.headline: Shared Or Divided?

scenes.narration: So on a lake with boats, fishing and holiday homes, there is no agreed border in the open water.
scenes.headline: Open Water, No Border

scenes.narration: People still get along fine, because the countries have separate agreements for shipping, fishing and safety.
scenes.headline: Rules For Boats

scenes.narration: Swim out from the shore and nobody can say for sure which country you are floating in.
scenes.headline: Which Country Is This?

scenes.narration: A lake with no border is odd, but a town that uses another country's money is even odder.
scenes.headline: Odd Money Next

scenes.narration: Number three: Büsingen am Hochrhein, a small German town that is completely surrounded by Switzerland on every side.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: Its people are German citizens, they have a German address, and they vote in German elections.
scenes.headline: Germans By Law

scenes.narration: But the town is inside the Swiss customs area, so Swiss francs are used there every day.
scenes.headline: Paying In Swiss Francs

scenes.narration: Its car number plates start with the letters BÜS, a special code that only this one town has.
scenes.headline: Plates Start With BÜS

scenes.narration: Old deals between rulers left this little town on the German side of the paperwork, and it never changed.
scenes.headline: Old Deals, Still Here

scenes.narration: Walk down a street there and you are in Germany, while the land and the money around you are Swiss.
scenes.headline: Germany, Swiss Money

scenes.narration: That is strange enough. But the next place has a village inside a village inside a country.
scenes.headline: A Village In A Village

scenes.narration: Number two: Madha, a patch of Oman that sits inside the United Arab Emirates.
scenes.headline: Madha

scenes.narration: Madha belongs to Oman but is cut off from it, with UAE land surrounding it on every side.
scenes.headline: Oman, Cut Off

scenes.narration: Now comes the twist. Inside Madha there is a tiny village called Nahwa, and Nahwa belongs to the UAE.
scenes.headline: Nahwa: UAE Again

scenes.narration: So you get UAE land, inside Omani land, inside UAE land. A country inside a country inside a country.
scenes.headline: Country In A Country

scenes.narration: On satellite maps the shapes look like a puzzle piece, and the border lines wrap around the village.
scenes.headline: A Puzzle On Satellite

scenes.narration: A short drive around this area can take you across the line between Oman and the UAE more than once.
scenes.headline: Cross The Line Twice

scenes.narration: Imagine your phone trying to decide which country you are in, every few minutes.
scenes.headline: Phone Gets Confused

scenes.narration: It is a beautiful puzzle, but it is still not the strangest border on this list.
scenes.headline: Still Not Number One

scenes.narration: For the strangest one, we are going home to India, and to the border with Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Now, India

scenes.narration: Number one: the India and Bangladesh border near Cooch Behar in West Bengal, which was cut into tiny pieces.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar Border

scenes.narration: For decades, small patches of land belonging to one country sat inside the other country, with no land link back home.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: There were Indian villages inside Bangladesh and Bangladeshi villages inside India. In all, there were 162 of these pockets.
scenes.headline: 162 Pockets

scenes.narration: These are called enclaves, and the people living in them were surrounded by a different country on every side.
scenes.headline: Surrounded On All Sides

scenes.narration: Many residents said it was hard to get schools, hospitals, and official papers, because their own country was not reachable.
scenes.headline: No Easy Access Home

scenes.narration: And one of those pockets was stranger than all the rest. It was called Dahala Khagrabari.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was a piece of India, inside a piece of Bangladesh, inside a piece of India, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: India, Bangladesh, Repeat

scenes.narration: That is four layers of borders around one patch of land, and no other place on Earth had so many.
scenes.headline: Four Layers Deep

scenes.narration: If you stood in the middle of it, you would have had to cross several borders just to reach mainland India.
scenes.headline: Cross Borders To Go Home

scenes.narration: In 2015, India and Bangladesh finally signed off on a land deal to end all of these pockets.
scenes.headline: The 2015 Deal

scenes.narration: At midnight on 31 July 2015, 111 Indian enclaves became part of Bangladesh, and 51 Bangladeshi ones became part of India.
scenes.headline: The Midnight Handover

scenes.narration: Residents were allowed to choose which country they wanted to belong to, after decades of living in the middle of nowhere.
scenes.headline: People Chose Their Country

scenes.narration: For many people, it meant a proper address, a vote, and a road to a school for the first time.
scenes.headline: An Address At Last

scenes.narration: So the strangest border in India was not a wall or a river. It was a puzzle drawn by history.
scenes.headline: A Puzzle By History

scenes.narration: That is why it is number one: a place with four borders around it, finally fixed in a single night.
scenes.headline: Number One, Fixed

scenes.narration: That was seven borders that make no sense, from a bridge where cars swap sides to a puzzle with four layers.
scenes.headline: All Seven Borders

scenes.narration: Remember the start: your car can switch sides of the road halfway across a bridge between Thailand and Laos.
scenes.headline: Back To The Bridge

scenes.narration: Tell me in the comments which border surprised you the most, and I will see you in the next video.
scenes.headline: Your Pick?

scenes.narration: Tomorrow, in the next video: the country with no border at its own front door.
scenes.headline: Next Video
scenes.sub: No border at its front door
